name: Between Rounds - By Oops to Opportunity
description:
Between Rounds is an evening for entrepreneurs, aspiring entrepreneurs and anyone curious about what it really takes to build something of their own.
Through honest, story-led conversations, our speakers unpack the uncertain decisions, difficult pivots and messy periods of growth that rarely make it into the success story.
Whether you are already building a business, still shaping an idea or simply wondering if entrepreneurship is for you, this is a room to learn from lived experience, ask better questions and meet others finding their way.

name: Sound of the Goddess - Chanting | Listening | Reflection
description:
Join Nina Rao (international chantress & seeker) and Neha Bhat (award winning author & sex therapist) for an intimate afternoon of chant, storytelling, and deep reflection on the Sacred Feminine. We'll be singing, reflecting and listening in-depth together!
About the Event
Join international chant leader Nina Rao and psychotherapist Neha Bhat for an intimate afternoon where ancient devotional traditions meet contemporary emotional understanding. Together, we will explore the many faces of the Divine Feminine through chant, reflection, and depth psychology.
Rather than looking at the stories of Devi as distant mythology, we will discover how they serve as living psychological wisdom, illuminating our modern experiences with grief, courage, boundaries, sexuality, healing, and belonging.
What to Expect
The afternoon will seamlessly weave together:
- Guided devotional chanting and mantra practice
- Reflective dialogue and storytelling
- Interactive audience conversation
- Contemplative practices and somatic insights
No prior experience with chanting or meditation is necessary. All are welcome.
About the Facilitators
Nina Rao brings the experiential, devotional, and embodied practice of mantra and Bhakti. Rooted in traditional chanting and years of teaching alongside Krishna Das, she speaks beautifully on the Sacred Feminine, nature, and contemplative practice.
Neha Bhat, ABT, ATR-P brings the lenses of contemporary psychology, sexual wellness, archetypal thinking, and the emotional landscapes of modern womanhood
Date: Thursday, November 5, 2026
Time: 3:00 PM – 5:30 PM
Ticket: ₹650 per person | You'll recieve a confirmation within two business days.
Simple refreshments will be provided.
For event related enquiries please email: assistant@chantkirtan.com

name: Sacred Music for Sacred Forests Concert - Save Wild Tigers and Their Habitats | Satsang | Kirtan
description:
Join us for an evening of kirtan, music, and satsang with Nina Rao and Friends to raise awareness and funds for saving wild tigers and their habitats across India - the Land of the Tiger.
India is the last viable habitat for wild tigers and one of the most biologically diverse regions in Eurasia.
Protecting this ecosystem means safeguarding not just tigers, but also elephants, langurs, deer, birds, rivers, plants, and the sacred balance of nature itself.
This concert is a celebration of India’s living tradition of honoring wildlife as sacred embodiments of Mother Earth. Through intentional prayer, chanting, and community, let us come together to protect nature and give thanks. We will also share a few words about some of the critical work being done to protect India’s wildlife and wild lands.
Schedule
- 6:30 PM – Doors open for general admission seating (Please bring your own pillow if you wish to sit on the floor; chairs are also provided at the venue)
- 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM – Sacred Music for Sacred Forests Concert with Nina Rao & Friends
About Nina Rao & Saving Wild Tigers
Nina Rao (via SavingWildTigers.org) has been supporting tiger conservation in India since 1998, guided by renowned conservationists including the late Valmik Thapar, Dr. K. Ullas Karanth, Dr. Krithi K. Karanth, and Dr. Dharmendra Khandal.
Where Your Funds Go
All funds raised from this concert will go directly to community-based conservation projects focused on human-wildlife co-existence. Proceeds will be distributed evenly to support the following charity partners:
- Centre for Wildlife Studies, Bengaluru (CWS India) & Tiger Watch: Funding critical, grassroots conservation efforts to protect tigers and foster safe coexistence between wildlife and local communities.
- Go Dharmic (The Dharma Forest): Supporting the massive rewilding initiative in the Sundarbans to plant mangroves, which restore natural habitats and shield coastal communities.
Community Support: We believe this sacred music should be accessible to all. If you wish to join but require financial assistance, please email us at sandip@godharmic.com to request a community discount code.

name: Flying Tigers - Vikalp Bengaluru Presents
description:
Flying Tigers
A film by Madhusree Dutta
105 minutes | 2026 | Bengali, English, Mandarin, German with English subtitles
About the Film:
The term Flying Tigers originates from a massive US military logistical operation connecting India and China across Himalayas during World War II. This story resurfaced after 70 years, when mother of the director was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and kept saying  - Close the Windows / Tiger is Coming. The film traces various renditions of flying tiger by permeating through memories of territories, wars, and infrastructure projects. Following the il-logic of Alzheimer’s disease the film insistently shifts between lenses and perspectives, and slides across locations.
About the Filmmaker:
Madhusree Dutta is a filmmaker, author and cultural producer living in India and Germany.
Her area of interest are hybridity within public and urban culture as well as documentary and archival practices. She is the founder and former director (1998 - 2016) of Majlis, a center for interdisciplinary art initiatives in Mumbai; and former artistic director (2018 - 2021) of Academy of the Arts of the World (Akademie der Künste der Welt), in Cologne, Germany.
With Flying Tigers Madhusree Dutta returns to filmmaking after twenty years.
The screening will be followed by a QnA session with Director, Madhusree Dutta.
About Vikalp Bengaluru:
Vikalp Bengaluru is a collective of documentary filmmakers screening the best in non-fiction films in Bengaluru for over two decades. Read more here - https://vikalpbengaluru.weebly.com/

name: The World in the Body: Observe. Absorb. Create. - A Workshop by Tushar Pandey
description:
The World in the Body: Observe. Absorb. Create.
A Workshop by Tushar Pandey
This workshop explores the immense possibilities of the performer’s body and mind, and the relationship between the body, space and the world around us. Through observation, physical exploration and play, participants will draw from the rhythms, movements, textures and dynamics of nature, objects, people and spaces, allowing these external influences to become internal impulses and material for performance.
The work moves between the external and the internal: what moves us, what creates an impulse, and how physical sensation can lead to emotion, sound, words and eventually images.
Imagination and physicality become tools for exploring different theatrical languages, from realistic text and dramatic composition to epic storytelling and grotesque or comic worlds.

name: Bhima
description:
Bhima
Language: English
Devised and performed by: Vivek Vijayakumaran and Sachin Gurjale
Directed by: Anitha Santhanam
Drawing inspiration from Ashok Malhotra’s Child Man, MT Vasudevan Nair’s Randamoozham, and Jeanette Winterson’s Weight, this play explores the paradoxes and ironies in the life of the second Pandava, Bhima.
Who is Bhima? What is his hunger? Who feeds it? What are the choices available to a hero? What is the fate of a strong man in contemporary times? These are some of the questions around which the key narrative of the play evolves. What is his relevance to contemporary life? Would his version of masculinity be acceptable in today’s world?
If Bhima were to live today, who would he be — a loyal middle-management warrior who is the engine of the company but never its CEO? A family man who defines himself only in terms of roles — the breadwinner, the husband, the son — who will do anything for his family? Or does he exist as an individual beyond these roles? Does society look after its Bhimas, or is it only Arjuna we want?
Contrasting the Koodiyattam form with contemporary dialogue and commentary, using music and poetry as interventions, Bhima re-examines a version of masculinity and its interaction with modernity.
Bhima won the Best Innovative Sound Design award for Sachin Gurjale at the 2017 Mahindra Excellence in Theatre Awards (META).

name: Physical Theatre: Its Possibilities and Limits - A Conversation with Tushar Pandey, Ashwath Bhatt and Vivek Vijayakumaran
description:
Physical Theatre: Its Possibilities and Limits
A Conversation with Tushar Pandey, Ashwath Bhatt and Vivek Vijayakumaran
Moderated by Anmol Vellani
Physical theatre communicates primarily, though not solely, through the language of gestures, facial expressions and movement. The exception is mime, which is non-verbal by definition.
In this session, three theatre artists will speak about what attracted them to physical theatre and describe the nature of their involvement in the teaching and practice of this stylised form of performance. As their work as directors and actors has also extended beyond physical theatre, they will reflect on the reasons for their divergent artistic choices.
Physical theatre has many strengths. Most notably, it can overcome language barriers, express what words cannot, connect with audiences at a visceral level, harness the ideas and creativity of the whole group, and rely on minimalist scenography. But equally, it is constrained by the very characteristics that set it apart from other theatre styles. This session will conclude with a discussion on the limits of physical theatre and the creative strategies that can prevent style from overshadowing substance.

name: Red Nose Clowning - A Workshop by Ashwath Bhatt - Nov 23
description:
Red Nose Clowning
A Workshop by Ashwath Bhatt
The clown often lands in a place where urgency prevails and dilemma takes over, pressure turns into perseverance and a never-say-die attitude emerges. The clown lives in the moment, in a theatre of the 'Here and Now'.
Through the clown, participants will explore the world from a more positive viewpoint, free from moral and logical constraints. We all have a clown hiding within us. During the workshop, an inner clown character will be born through an organic process based on both eastern and western techniques. Starting with an outer neutral persona, we will work our way towards the ridiculous and then the grotesque.
At the end of the workshop, participants will gain clarity about the rules and tools of clowning, so that they can embark on clown exploration with courage. The workshop will go beyond gags and look for the clown who connects to the heart of the spectators.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Sustainable Theatre Practice - A Workshop by Pratiksha Khasnis and Kalpesh Samel - Nov 23
description:
Sustainable Theatre Practice
A Workshop by Pratiksha Khasnis and Kalpesh Samel
This is an interactive workshop that draws from different experiences of running and touring with an independent theatre company. Through theatre games, group exercises, improvisation and practical discussions, participants will explore ways of creating, producing, touring and sustaining a theatre with limited resources. The workshop will look at audience-building, working collaboratively, mobility, and developing practical models that are both artistically meaningful and financially viable.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Uncle Dance
description:
Uncle Dance
Language: Hindi, English
Conceived and performed by: Pranjal Vaid with Jai Prakash Kumar
Age Limit: Above 18 years
Uncle Dance borrows from Pranjal’s personal struggles with patriarchy and with dance. It enquires into the quintessential uncle and the role of power and security in relationships and on the dance floor. The play also explores marriage as a construct, and the possibility of two people tying the knot to become one, when they are always actually two.

name: Lecture-Demonstration on the Folk Theatre of Bayalata - An Experience Sharing Session by Dr. Sahana Pinjar
description:
Lecture-Demonstration on the Folk Theatre of Bayalata
An Experience Sharing Session by Dr. Sahana Pinjar
Dr. Sahana Pinjar will be presenting a live demonstration of the traditional Kannada folk-theatre form of Bayalata through the performance of Girija Kalyana, depicting the divine marriage of Girija (Parvati) and Lord Shiva.  The demonstration will showcase the storytelling, acting, dialogue, traditional movements, music, costumes, and theatrical conventions of Bayalata, bringing the story to life for a contemporary audience. The story, written by Dr. Basavaraja Malshati, portrays Girija’s deep devotion and determination to attain Lord Shiva, her penance, and the eventual divine wedding. Through lively characters, expressive acting, traditional music and the energetic style of Bayalata, the narrative unfolds as both a sacred tale and a vibrant theatrical experience.
The performance celebrates themes of devotion, love, perseverance and the union of divine energies, while preserving the distinctive visual and performative elements of Karnataka’s folk theatre tradition.
For queries contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com
